title: Direct oral anticoagulants vs VKA for recurrent VTE in acute symptomatic venous thromboembolism
question: In adults with acute symptomatic venous thromboembolism (VTE), do direct oral anticoagulants change recurrent VTE versus warfarin / vitamin-K antagonist therapy?
eligibility_summary: RCT; adults with acute symptomatic VTE (DVT and/or PE) by title/registry conditions; DOAC (dabigatran, rivaroxaban, apixaban, or edoxaban) vs warfarin / VKA / conventional anticoagulant therapy; P/I/C/design only. Exclude cancer-only, thrombophilia-only, pediatric, extended/secondary-prevention, and placebo/aspirin comparator trials.

primary_outcome.name: Trial-reported recurrent VTE composite
primary_outcome.timepoint: trial end / longest randomized acute-treatment follow-up

estimand_exclusions.their_outcome: Recurrent VTE during extended therapy after 6-12 months of prior anticoagulation
estimand_exclusions.reason: Wrong comparator and phase of therapy: rivaroxaban vs placebo for extended/secondary prevention, not DOAC vs warfarin / VKA for acute symptomatic VTE.

comparator_scope_note: van Es et al. 2014 (PMID 24963045) is a scope-matched open-access pooled analysis of the six phase-3 acute symptomatic VTE DOAC-vs-VKA trials and reports recurrent VTE including VTE-related death as RR 0.90 (0.77-1.06). van der Hulle et al. 2014 (PMID 24330006) was checked first because it is the canonical JTH systematic review/meta-analysis, but Unpaywall reported open_access=false during the build, so it was not used as the gate comparator. The trial pool here discloses mixed trial-reported ratio measures (five HRs and one RR) and a small outcome-definition difference: RE-COVER, RE-COVER II, and AMPLIFY include VTE-related death in the recurrent-VTE composite, whereas the EINSTEIN and Hokusai reports count recurrent VTE as reported. The EINSTEIN placebo extension embedded in PMID 21128814 is explicitly excluded as a wrong-comparator substudy.
